Multiple imputation by predictive mean matching

Source: R/mipmm.R
mipmm.Rd

Fills the missing values of numeric columns m times by predictive mean matching, each completed data set from its own chain of chained equations, and pools an analysis of the completed data sets by Rubin's rules: the step after mcartst() has said how the values are missing. Predictive mean matching imputes only values that were observed, so an imputed count stays a whole number and an imputed age stays in its range (van Buuren 2018, sec. 3.4).

Usage

mipmm(
  data,
  y,
  x = NULL,
  m = 5,
  k = 5,
  maxit = 5,
  ridge = 1e-05,
  fy = NULL,
  fx = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'mipmm'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit.

y

The names of the numeric columns to impute (missing values as NA; observed values finite).

x

NULL or the names of complete numeric columns that predict them; for print(), an object of class mipmm.

m

The imputations: a whole number from 2 to 1000.

k

The donors to draw from: a whole number from 1 to 10000.

maxit

The rounds of each chain: a whole number from 1 to 1000.

ridge

The ridge, as a share of the diagonal: a number from 0.

fy

NULL or the outcome of the analysis: a column of y or x.

fx

NULL or its predictors: columns of y or x other than fy.

level

The level of the intervals: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

seed

NULL (drawn from R's generator, so set.seed() fixes it) or a whole number from 0 to 2147483647.

...

Not used by print().

Value

An object of class mipmm, a list: imp, for each column of y a matrix of its imputed values, one row per missing value (named by its row of data) and one column per imputation; pool, a data frame (term, est, se, df, lo, hi, p, riv, fmi); nmis, the missing values of each column; and m, k, maxit, seed.

Details

Each chain starts the missing values of every column of y at draws from its observed values and, maxit times, imputes each column in turn from all the others (the other columns of y as last imputed, and the complete columns x): the least squares fit on its observed rows, ridge times the diagonal of the cross-products added to it; a draw of the residual scale (rss over a chi-square on the residual degrees of freedom) and of the coefficients about their estimate; and, for each missing row, a donor drawn with equal chances among the k observed rows whose fitted values (from the estimate) are nearest its own (from the draw), whose observed value it takes (van Buuren 2018, sec. 4.5; type 1 matching). The draws come from the package's generator.

The analysis is the least squares fit of fy on an intercept and fx (classical variances), or, without fy, the mean of each column of y (variance s^2 / n). Pooled by Rubin (1987): est the mean of the m estimates, se the square root of T = U + (1 + 1 / m) B (U the mean variance, B the variance between imputations), df that of Barnard and Rubin (1999) with the complete-data degrees of freedom of the analysis, Student's t interval and p-value, riv the relative increase in variance (1 + 1 / m) B / U and fmi the fraction of missing information, as the mice package pools.

References

van Buuren, S. (2018). Flexible Imputation of Missing Data, 2nd ed. Chapman and Hall/CRC. doi:10.1201/9780429492259

Rubin, D. B. (1987). Multiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys. Wiley. doi:10.1002/9780470316696

Barnard, J. and Rubin, D. B. (1999). Small-sample degrees of freedom with multiple imputation. Biometrika, 86(4), 948-955. doi:10.1093/biomet/86.4.948

Little, R. J. A. (1988). Missing-data adjustments in large surveys. Journal of Business and Economic Statistics, 6(3), 287-296. doi:10.1080/07350015.1988.10509663

Examples

set.seed(11)
n <- 200
d <- data.frame(age = round(runif(n, 18, 60)), male = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5))
d$priors <- rpois(n, exp(-1 + 0.04 * d$age))
d$days <- round(20 + 3 * d$priors + 5 * d$male + rnorm(n, sd = 5))
d$priors[sample(n, 40)] <- NA
d$days[sample(n, 30)] <- NA
r <- mipmm(d, c("priors", "days"), c("age", "male"), fy = "days",
           fx = c("priors", "male"), seed = 1)
r
#> mipmm: 70 missing value(s) in 2 column(s), 5 imputations by predictive mean matching
#>         term    est     se    df     lo     hi         p    riv    fmi
#>  (Intercept) 18.629 0.8058 40.95 17.002 20.257 4.065e-25 0.3591 0.2977
#>       priors  3.432 0.2773 27.11  2.863  4.001 1.154e-12 0.5178 0.3849
#>         male  6.242 0.8145 61.78  4.614  7.871 1.550e-10 0.2468 0.2227
head(r$imp$priors)
#>    [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5]
#> 11    2    1    0    1    0
#> 17    0    1    2    0    2
#> 18    1    0    0    3    2
#> 19    0    0    0    0    2
#> 21    1    1    3    1    1
#> 23    0    1    0    0    0
